title: Leading software factories and agent-platform architectures
purpose: Research input for the Agent OS architecture review: what leading autonomous software factories and general agent platforms do, what works, what fails, and what Agent OS can learn. Questions are posed identically to every arm.
context_for_judges: The reader operates Agent OS, a self-hosted OS for an agent fleet. It has a Postgres session ledger, governed multi-harness worker dispatch (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini), build packs (spec -> DAG -> tickets -> PRs), cross-model adversarial review bound to the PR head, autonomous merge, self-deploy with smoke tests, and a SEV -> postmortem -> hardening-ledger 'scar memory' re-injected into worker prompts. It wants to become a general-purpose platform for agentic systems (marketing teams, business automation, content factories). An insight is valuable when it is a specific, verifiable fact, design detail, measured result or failure mode that would change an architecture decision, not a generic claim or marketing adjective.

questions.text: How does StrongDM's 'Software Factory' work, where no human writes or reviews code? What are its scenario holdouts and digital twin universe, how is correctness verified, and what results or problems have been reported?

What is the architecture of Factory.ai's Droids: execution environment, context and memory, how tasks are delegated, and how output is verified? What do engineering write-ups or benchmarks say about results?

How do Cognition's Devin and Windsurf run long autonomous coding sessions (sandbox, planning, sessions, knowledge, playbooks)? What do published customer case studies report about merge rates and failure modes?

How does OpenAI Codex cloud run agent tasks: sandbox containers, AGENTS.md, parallel tasks, review, and internet access policy? What has OpenAI published about how it uses Codex internally and the measured results?

How do the GitHub Copilot coding agent and GitHub Agent HQ / Mission Control orchestrate multiple vendors' coding agents? Cover the execution environment (Actions runners), firewall, review and merge flow, and governance controls.

How does Stripe's 'Minions' system produce unattended pull requests at scale? Cover the devbox and sandbox model, the blueprint/workflow mix of deterministic and agentic steps, CI and review, and volume numbers.

What have Ramp, Spotify (Honk / Fleet Management), Shopify, Uber, Airbnb or Meta published about their internal background coding agents or fleet-wide automated code migrations? Include architecture, verification approach and measured outcomes.

What does Anthropic recommend for long-running agent harnesses and multi-agent systems? Cover initializer and coding agents, progress files, context compaction, subagents, the Claude Agent SDK, Agent Skills, and the multi-agent research system's lessons on token cost and orchestration.

What are the architectures and reported results of open-source autonomous coding agents and frameworks: OpenHands (All Hands), SWE-agent / mini-swe-agent, Block's goose, and Sourcegraph Amp? Focus on the agent-computer interface, sandboxing, and lessons from SWE-bench-style evaluation.

What is spec-driven development as implemented by Amazon Kiro, GitHub Spec Kit and similar tools? How are specs, plans and tasks structured, and what evidence is there that it improves agent output quality?

How are durable-execution engines (Temporal, Restate, Inngest, DBOS) used to run AI agents reliably? What patterns do they recommend for retries, human-in-the-loop waits, long-running workflows, and idempotent tool calls, and which companies run agents on them in production?

Compare the general-purpose agent platforms: LangGraph Platform, CrewAI, Microsoft Agent Framework (AutoGen + Semantic Kernel), OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK / Vertex Agent Engine, and AWS Bedrock AgentCore. Cover runtime, state and memory, deployment, identity and auth, observability, and how multi-agent systems are composed.

What 'operating system for agents' designs exist (AIOS, Letta/MemGPT, others)? How do they handle scheduling, memory management, context switching, tool access and isolation between agents, and what has been learned from them?

How are MCP and A2A being used as extension seams for agent platforms in production? What are the known problems: tool-count limits, auth and authorization (OAuth for MCP), security incidents like prompt injection via tools, and gateway or registry patterns that address them?

How do production agent platforms authorize agents to act on behalf of users and organizations? Cover policy engines (Cedar, OPA, OpenFGA / Zanzibar-style ReBAC) applied to agents, scoped short-lived credentials, agent identity standards, and approval gates for irreversible actions.

What sandboxing approaches are used for autonomous agents (Firecracker microVMs, gVisor, e2b, Modal, Daytona, Cloudflare, devcontainers)? Compare startup time, isolation strength, snapshot/resume, cost, and network egress control, with any published benchmarks.

How do teams verify autonomous agent output without human code review: eval-driven development, scenario or holdout tests, property-based tests, LLM-as-judge, cross-model review, and digital twins of external services? What evidence exists on how well each catches defects?

What are the documented failure modes of autonomous AI coding agents at scale: reward hacking or test tampering, review rubber-stamping, regressions introduced by fixes, runaway token spend, and merge conflicts in high-volume repos? How do organizations mitigate them?

How do organizations govern token and compute cost for agent fleets: budgets per task or agent, model routing and cascades, prompt caching, and cost attribution? What figures have been published for the cost per merged PR or per completed agent task?

What AI SRE / self-healing systems exist (for example Resolve.ai, Cleric, Traversal, PagerDuty and Datadog agents, Meta's or Google's internal remediation)? How do they detect, diagnose, remediate and verify, and what autonomy levels and safety controls do they use?

How do merge queues and stacked-PR systems (GitHub merge queue, Graphite, Aviator, Mergify, Bors-style) handle very high PR volume from agents? What is known about throughput, CI cost and conflict rates when agents open hundreds of PRs a day?

Beyond coding, what multi-agent systems run marketing, content production, sales or back-office automation in production? Cover architecture, human approval points, brand and quality control, and measured results, and say which are built on general agent platforms rather than bespoke code.

How do agent systems capture and reuse lessons from past failures: incident memory, playbooks, learned rules injected into prompts, and self-improving agents? What evidence is there that this reduces repeat failures, and what are the risks (prompt bloat, stale rules)?
What notable autonomous software factory or agent platform announcements, architectures or postmortems were published between September and November 2026?
